ctx.x: Mary Brunus, Denise, Abby Brunus, Georgie Brunus.
It looks like they got a bottle of muscatel. That Harry Shields?

Yeah. No, no, she ain't there. No, no, that's Joe Moranison. Looks like Joe Moranison. Looks like Joe Moranison. I can't see so well. I know Head Brunus was in that bunch, I believe, the day they came in.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: I picked them boys up playing with me when they were just small children.

ctx.x: I sure did, lots of them.
I see. Now, another thing, too. Do you remember Tom Brown and Harry Shields when they used to play in the old days?
Yes, I do remember. I picked them boys up playing with me when they were just small children.

items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: I think I played only one job with him.

ctx.x: Larry, yeah. That's where he left.

We saw Jack Lane on Friday. They took a television movie for the educational television station. He's going to have a little interview and movie with him some of these days on there. Yeah. He's in good health, looked pretty good. He does. His wife is all right too, but she has trouble with her legs now. Oh, she does. He can't walk very well. Did you ever get to play with Papa Lane yourself?

I think I played only one job with him. Well, I was really playing with his son. With his son. His son played cornet, but he happened to play bass drum. I think we played a parade one day. Georgie Brunas was playing some wrong, and I think Emmet Rogers played the snare drum that day, and Jack played bass drum. Of course, we were kids then.
